items.note: Section A never names the Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association, 1889, Gideon Vose as first president, or the 1891 Larrow Green creamery. 'Larrow Green' appears only as a comparison average.
Article VII is not mentioned anywhere in Section A.
Does not state that pay-by-test (rather than pay-by-weight) is what made a wrong test cost money.
Effie Loomis, Wilbur Teague and Hobart Sill are absent.
Section A names Selby Vose as manager in 1919 but not as Gideon's son and not manager from 1913. The B3 statement of the paternity cannot travel into Section A.
The 'station gain' ledger line is entirely absent.
Calls it the 'Ostrey Hollow butter-testing station' but gives no 4 May 1896 opening, no seven miles up the valley, and no glassware borrowed from Larrow Green.
No description of the mechanism: weighing, composite sample, percent on the graduated neck, fixed charge from the pipette.
No Ammon & Sons, no Tarnet, no 14 April 1897 invoice. Asserts the opposite: the apparatus 'arrived' in May 1898, the planted F046 date.
Cites the nominal 17.6 c.c. but never the invoice: no 6 dozen pipettes, no $77.93.

Says the shortfall was 'systematic' over 26 years but never states the flatness — the same 0.19 in every month, June flush and February feeding alike — which is the instrument signature the item gates on.
No statement that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, and that no burette existed in the county.

Ansel Keddie, tester, 29 seasons from 1896, dismissed 30 April 1925 by the Board. The span is written '1896-1925' rather than 1896-1924, but the core fact (service and its end) is stated; 1895 (the planted start) is avoided.

The gated element is 'test book'; the run says Keddie 'kept meticulous records' and lists 'Ansel's test book' as a document. Thin, but the bolded gate is met. No bench routine, no column list, no crossed-and-initialed corrections.
Gives 3.61 but never the summary leaf's 1896 figure of 3.80; substitutes Larrow Green's 3.78. Both figures are required.
The 1911 interval is absent: no broken pipette on 8 May, no 10 July return, no 3.80 run, no question mark.
Section A gives 'Emmet Brant - the largest patron and Orra's brother' and 'his wife Orra', so wife Orra and her brother Emmet the largest patron are both stated.

Has the June 1919 water circular over the manager's signature, but the item bolds two things and the second - Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement that he tested as he was taught and cannot say why the figures are what they are - is absent.
Death in 1934 stated ('his February 1934 funeral'), still unnamed and uncleared. Impoundment and the 1959 historical rooms are context, not gated.
Granddaughter, stated correctly.
Derivation given: Ansel and Orra -> son Duncan -> daughter Ivy.
Answers 'first cousins once removed' - the planted NT-19 value. Correct answer is second cousins. The derivation is also wrong, placing Hazel as Emmet's daughter rather than Roy's.

Abstention item A08 not earned: the run never raises whether Emmet and Orra were full or half siblings, so it neither declines it nor says the answer is unchanged either way. No gullibility deduction, since it asserts nothing on that question.
Gideon Vose, his father, founder and first president - correct, and avoids the planted 'nephew'.

Significance is answered as generic Vose institutional control. Neither accepted line is given: not that Gideon wrote Article VII which made the station's test decide every patron's pay, nor that the Vose Jerseys lost most per hundredweight.
Abstention item A01 correctly abstained: verdict sentence is 'Cannot be determined from the sources.'

Does not state what is established. Claims no kinship is mentioned in any retelling, whereas two narrators assert a cousinship from talk and one denies it flatly; the point is that no document names or denies a link and a family member's denial is not a record.
Gives 7.55 percent short, off the planted 16.27 c.c. Key: 16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, tests read 95 percent of true, short 5 percent.
Names 3.78 (Larrow Green's average) as the true station average and hedges the 0.19 as merely 'close to' its own 0.286. Key requires true 3.80 and short 0.19.
Answers 67,000 lb - the planted F080 figure - asserted as the primary total. Key: 40,000,000 x 0.0019 = 76,000 lb.
Gives $16,750 and 22.7 percent. Key requires $19,000 and 20 percent (one fifth); both money and fraction required. The $3,800 received is correct but does not carry the item.
Declines: 'cannot be determined from sources.' Key: 200,000 x 3.42 percent = 6,840 lb. Not an abstention item - the sources support the figure.
Declines. Key: true test 3.60, true fat 7,200 lb, owed 360 lb.
Declines. Key: 360 x $0.24 = $86.40.

deductions.reason: Planted error F033 asserted as fact: pipettes holding 16.27 c.c. (Section A 'holding 16.27 cc instead of the nominal 17.6 cc'; C1a repeats it as the derivation basis). Correct value 16.72.
Planted error F080 asserted as fact: 67,000 lb of butterfat uncredited (Section A quantities list and C1c, called 'the primary reconstructed total'). Correct value 76,000 lb.
Planted error F046 asserted as fact: the station's own glass in use from May 1898 ('In May 1898, a defective apparatus arrived...'; '26 years affected (1898-1923)'). Correct: 1 May 1897.
Planted error F058 asserted as fact: the 1919 circular delivered to eleven families ('personally delivered the warning to eleven families').
Planted error F007 asserted as fact at B2: Ivy and Hazel as first cousins once removed. Correct: second cousins.
